summary: Tested the Hyperliquid SPOT integration end to end, backend and frontend, using demo.team1. Backend (pytest, 9 tests): 6 passed, 3 failed. Pairs, validation, demo bind/get/unbind, the demo BUY->SELL cycle on SOLUSDT and blocking Hyperliquid while Binance is bound all work. The 3 failures are one gap in the one-exchange-per-account rule: the Binance, KuCoin and LBank bind endpoints do not check for an existing Hyperliquid binding, so any of them can be added while Hyperliquid is connected. Frontend (430px viewport): every requested UI check passed, including demo bind and unbind through the UI. The account was left with no exchange bound.

critical.issue: These endpoints do not check db.hyperliquid_keys. With Hyperliquid bound in demo, each of them returned 200 and bound a second exchange. This breaks the one-exchange-per-account rule. _execute_trade then silently routes by priority lbank > kucoin > hyperliquid > binance. Fix: add `if await db.hyperliquid_keys.find_one({'user_id': user['id']}): raise HTTPException(400, 'Hyperliquid is already connected... Disconnect Hyperliquid first...')` to all three bind handlers (around lines 699, 775 and 920).

minor.issue: Demo transactions have no 'exchange' field, while the real Hyperliquid path sets exchange='hyperliquid'. The demo price also comes from Binance (85.66), not the Hyperliquid mid (85.60). The design allows this, but the history cannot show which exchange a demo trade belongs to.

Synchronous SDK network calls run inside async code and block the event loop: _hl_resolve_pair -> info.spot_meta() (cold cache), _hl_price -> info.all_mids(), the _HLInfo(...) constructor (which fetches meta) in get_user_hyperliquid and in hyperliquid_bind, and _HLExchange(...). Wrap them in run_in_threadpool, or cache the Info and Exchange objects per network.

Binding only checks that the address can be reached through spot_user_state. It does not check that the agent key is actually approved for the account, so a wrong agent key binds fine and fails later at order time. Consider checking info.query_user_to_multi_sig_signers or the extraAgents list, or placing a tiny dry-run order.

ui_bugs.issue: The badge shows 'Live' only when mode==='real'. A testnet binding shows 'Demo', while the connected card's isLive treats testnet as live. Minor inconsistency that also exists for the other exchanges.

verified_working: /bind-api: Hyperliquid is row #9 with tag 'No-KYC · Non-custodial Spot' and a blue Bind button; KuCoin is #10

/bind-api/hyperliquid: green safety card, no Server IP/whitelist card, Demo/Testnet/Real modes, 'Main Wallet Address' input, 'Agent API Key' label with placeholder 'Agent / API key (trade-only)', no 'Private Key' text
Switching to Testnet and Real shows the Hyperliquid-specific warnings

UI demo bind shows the toast 'Hyperliquid connected successfully' and the API Bound card '0xa1a1…a1a1 · DEMO'; the list row then shows 'Demo'; clicking Binance shows 'Please disconnect Hyperliquid first'; UI unbind shows 'API unbound'
GET /api/hyperliquid/pairs returns the 6 pairs (@142, @151, @156, @107, @162, @188) with non-zero prices
Invalid address in real mode returns 400 mentioning 0x; invalid agent key in real mode returns 400
Demo bind sets active_exchange=hyperliquid; unbind resets it to binance; agent_key_enc is not exposed
Demo BUY 20 USDT then SELL on SOLUSDT both return transactions that are persisted in /transactions; bot.exchange is self-healed to hyperliquid
Hyperliquid bind is blocked (400) when Binance is bound
action_items: Add a Hyperliquid-already-connected check to the POST /binance/bind, /kucoin/bind and /lbank/bind handlers
Optional: add exchange='hyperliquid' to demo transactions when the routed exchange is Hyperliquid
Optional: move the synchronous Hyperliquid SDK calls off the event loop with run_in_threadpool
critical_code_review_comments: The one-exchange rule is only enforced in one direction for Hyperliquid (see the critical issue above)
Blocking SDK I/O in async paths (_hl_price, _hl_resolve_pair, Info/Exchange constructors)
server.py is about 6900 lines; the Hyperliquid code should move into its own module

success_rate.backend: 67% (6/9; the 3 failures are one issue across 3 endpoints)

seed_data_creation: None kept. The test creates temporary Binance/KuCoin/LBank demo bindings and Hyperliquid demo bindings on demo.team1, and removes them in the same test. It also adds 2 demo SOLUSDT transactions (BUY+SELL, about +$0.007 profit).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run with: REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=... pytest tests/test_hyperliquid_integration.py -n 0 (it must run serially because all tests share one account). The test_other_blocked_when_hl_bound cases should pass once the reverse checks are added. Real or testnet Hyperliquid fills cannot be tested without a funded wallet.
